scenario: AITA for asking my pregnant SIL to leave the family Christmas gathering? | Okay so based on title I totally sound like an asshole but hear me out. So this year is our turn to host the family Christmas party at our home. We invited not only my SOs side but also my side as well. Overall it was around 20ish people in our home today for gift giving and typical American Christmas celebrating. Drinks were shared, food broken, the whole shebang. Amongst my SOs side of the family was his pregnant sister. She, I think, was due maybe a week or so ago? But really its just been ticking time bomb for her little one to arrive. Everybodys excited to meet the baby! Now our problem is that SIL came to the party with contractions and was obviously in labor (I know this because Im a mom myself - once you know, you know). Every 20 minutes or so she would start having pains and would make noises to pass the contractions. At first it wasnt so bad; I understand how sucky it is and you dont want to go to the hospital too soon because they'll just send you right home. But then it became almost obnoxious. I feel terrible for saying that but it really was. A lot of my family members and some of hers were glancing around like WTF? Go home and do that in private. After a while it became apparent that it was making everybody uncomfortable and even my MIL reccommend that she rest at home before it gets too late. She refused and said she was fine. In the middle of the kids opening their presents she went into pain again and this time she even screamed for a second. I then discreetly pulled her husband to the side and told them to leave. I did it politely ("Hey I appreciate you guys for being here but I think its time to go. I dont want you guys to give birth in our kitchen! lol"). After I said that her husband got angry and quickly got her and the kids packed up. She visibly upset and before heading out called me a bitch and said that I ruined Christmas for her. A few of their sides family members gave me dirty looks and left soon after. Im torn on this: I wanted everybody to have a good day but it was very distracting and obnoxious to have her around. I feel bad but still. tl;dr -- I asked SIL to leave family Christmas party because she was in labor.

Let me break this down step by step. First, the scenario: They're hosting a family Christmas party with around 20 people. The SIL is pregnant, due in a week or so, and she comes to the party with contractions. At first, it's manageable, but as time goes on, her contractions become more frequent and noticeable, to the point where she's screaming in pain during the kids' present-opening. The person hosting, who's a man, feels that her presence is becoming disruptive and making everyone uncomfortable. He politely asks her to leave, which upsets her and some of her family members, leading to some tension. So, the question is: Was it right or wrong for him to ask her to leave? I think the first thing to consider is the well-being of the SIL and her baby. If she's in active labor, she should be at the hospital. The host recognized that she was in labor, which is a serious situation. By asking her to leave, he was essentially telling her to go to the hospital, which is the appropriate place for her to be. That part seems responsible. On the other hand, the party was a family gathering meant for celebration. The host had put effort into hosting, and the SIL's presence was causing a lot of disruption. The noise from her contractions was making people uncomfortable, and it was distracting from the festivities. The host's intention was to ensure that everyone, including the SIL, could have a good day. However, her condition was making that difficult. Another angle is the social dynamics. The host's actions led to some family members being upset, and the SIL called him a name and left. It's possible that the host could have handled the situation more sensitively. Maybe instead of asking her to leave, he could have offered to take her to the hospital himself or called an Uber for her. That might have been a kinder approach without causing as much offense. But then again, the host was in a position where he had to manage the party. He had to consider the comfort of all the guests, not just the SIL. If her contractions were becoming too disruptive, it's understandable that he wanted to resolve the situation quickly to maintain the atmosphere of the gathering. I also think about the potential risks. If the SIL was in active labor, staying at the party could have been dangerous. The host was probably concerned for her and the baby's safety, which is a valid reason to ask her to leave. However, the way he approached her might have been a bit harsh. He told her husband to leave, which could have come off as insensitive. Maybe a more empathetic approach, like expressing concern for her well-being and suggesting they go to the hospital, would have been better received. In the end, while his intention was to ensure everyone's comfort and safety, the method he used might have been the issue. It's a tough spot to be in, balancing the needs of the family and the immediate medical situation. I think he did the right thing in recognizing the urgency, but perhaps the way he handled it could have been more considerate.
